narrative_purpose: Makes the material trick visible: a cutaway of a Pandoran limb bone showing the lattice of dark carbon fibre threaded through pale bone, lighter and stronger than Earth bone - the single innovation that lets the pa'li keep slender legs and the ikran fly hollow.
subject: A clean cross-section cutaway of a long limb bone, sliced to reveal the interior: a thin outer wall of pale bone, hollow at the core, with a fine three-dimensional lattice of dark carbon-like fibres woven through the wall like rebar in concrete. The wall is conspicuously thinner than a solid mammal bone would be, the holey lightweight structure clearly readable.
scene: An abstract dark specimen space, the bone section floating and lit as if for study, deep haze beyond.
camera: A near three-quarter view into the cut face so both the hollow core and the fibre lattice in the wall are visible, the section sharp.
light: Cool study light raking across the cut face plus a faint bioluminescent glow from within the porous bone; deep indigo shadow.
palette: Void-indigo ground, pale bone-grey and teal on the section, darker threads for the carbon fibre, faint cyan glow in the pores, one scarce amber pinpoint.
style: Painterly naturalist specimen plate, hand-painted texture, museum-cutaway clarity.
detail_level: Crisp on the cut face - the thin wall, the hollow core, the woven fibre lattice; background dissolving into haze.
composition: A single bone section set slightly off-centre, the cut face turned to the viewer, generous dark negative space, 16:9.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette with bioluminescent key from within the bone. Same dark glowing-specimen mood as the chapter cover and the pa'li plate.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no cartoon or anime style
